newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cisi buy will not dilute Signaux earnings.
newsitem.headline: Cisi buy will not dilute Signaux earnings.

text.p: An acquisition of French computer systems house Cisi will not dilute earnings of Cie de Signaux, the latter's chairman, Yazid Sabeg, said on Monday.

"I do not think the effects will be dilutive on the results of Signaux," he said at a news conference. He declined to give financing details of the deal, announced earlier in March and in which state-owned CEA-Industrie is selling its 64-percent stake to electronics firm Signaux.
He simply said Signaux would financially and industrially restructure Cisi, which has made losses for a number of years and reported a 1995 net loss of around 120 million francs.
Cisi should return to profit at the operating level in 1998, Signaux said.
Sabeg estimated Cisi's overstaffing at 250 and compulsory redundancies should be limited to about 10 positions.
He said talks had begun on Signaux buying the 34 percent of Cisi held by Cap Gemini. "We are buyers of Cap Gemini's holding and they are sellers," he said.
Cap Gemini said in February it was a potential seller of its Cisi stake.
A planned acquisition of Cisi by the Franco-British Sema Group failed last year.
Cisi had 1996 turnover of 1.15 billion francs and employed 1,900 people.
